name: Sergius
overview: Sergius Paulus was a male figure known as the proconsul of Cyprus, a significant Roman administrative title indicating his role as a chief magistrate governing the island. Scripture identifies him specifically in Acts 13:7, but no further personal or tribal details are provided. His position highlights his importance in the early Christian narrative as a Roman official.
namesAndTitles: The name recorded is Sergius Paulus, which is presented plainly without any given meaning or special significance in the biblical text. This proper name is the sole designation attributed to him in Acts 13:7.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Sergius Paulus beyond his official role as proconsul. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Sergius Paulus is notable in the biblical narrative as a Roman proconsul who encountered the early Christian message during the apostolic mission in Cyprus. His inclusion in Acts 13:7 underscores the reach of the gospel into the Roman administrative structure and highlights the early church's engagement with influential leaders. His role serves as a testament to the gospel's power to impact individuals in positions of authority.
